Here is a recent drawing I made to explain my updated strategy for trading price's RT to a previous FO.

Something interesting I just thought of: the FO of the LFL in the drawing and subsequent low confirms the original LFL as an "inner FL" or "inner kink".

This ties in nicely with what I was practicing yesterday when I said price engulfs, then forms FO

If applied to this drawing, the LFL or "inner kink" is also and engulf, which precedes the FO.

The tricky part is verifying that the "engulf" has a valid unmet target. If so, you are clear to trade price's RT to the FO that forms as part of the 'outer kink'. But, if the target of the engulf (inner kink) is already met, the "FO" of the inner kink is actually an engulf. Why? Because price has no reason to FO if price is coming from a met target. Any breach of a level (if price is coming from a met target) is indicative of future price direction (it's not a trick; it's an engulf). When price is coming from an unmet target the breached levels are FO's...tricks are needed because there is an unmet target. If you miss this detail, the trade will fail. This is a new concept for me, so please don't accept this as being 100% accurate....but it's certainly worth thinking about.

The next drawing is similar to the one I just posted above, but this time I am showing a progression where a FO forms along with a new low, confirming the formation of an outer FL/kink. Notice, the FO is a "FO" only because it forms while the preceding engulf has yet to meet its target.

OK, the drawing below shows a situation where the engulf hits its target before the "FO forms". If this happens, I would label the area in the brown circle as an engulf...not a FO.

I am working on a way for spotting potential opportunities midway through the setup by identifying higher TF candles that reflect two lower TF FO's.

This will cut down on the time I spend scanning the charts for a setup. I'll be able to cover more pairs, more effectively. That's why I was posting the 'naked charts' on my post above...I am curious to see what twin fakeouts look like on a higher time frame chart.

Trading is hard & time consuming...we should always be focused on finding ways to make it simpler...as long as we don't sacrifice our discipline and core methodology.

In my opinion, half of the battle to being profitable as a trader is understanding what to look for...but the other half is being able to find it while the market is live and execute the trade properly with the right mental focus. It's easy to miss setups..time management is critically important. It is also important to develop an efficient method of drawing up your charts and tracking PA as it unfolds in real time.
